newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND TO INVITE BIDS PBK SA BANK ON JAN 31.
newsitem.headline: POLAND TO INVITE BIDS PBK SA BANK ON JAN 31.

text.p: The Polish finance ministry will invite bids for no less than 10 percent and no more than 65 percent of the commercial Powszechny Bank Kredytowy SA in a newspaper advertisement on January 31, the ministry said.
It said in a Thursday statement the deadline for bids was February 10 and that the finance ministry expected negotiations with shortlisted investors to be concluded at the end of April.

"After the end of negotiations with an investor or investors, the finance ministry will begin the second stage of the bank's privatisation through a public offering, which is expected in autumn this year," the statement said.
HSBC Investment Services, advising Poland in the privatisation of its PBK estimates its value at 1.2-1.6 billion zlotys.
The head of HSBC's Polish unit Hubert Janiszewski told Reuters 30 percent of PBK will be earmarked for the public offering of which up to 15 percent will be offered to the bank's employees.
The treasury will retain five percent for a programme to compensate former owners for property confiscated under communist rule.

The net profit of PBK jumped 78 percent to 215.3 million zlotys in 1996. It expects a pre-tax profit of 420-430 million zlotys in 1997, up from 370.3 million in 1996, which in turn was 46 percent higher than in 1995.
PBK's balance sheet total grew 24 percent in 1996 to 9.8 billion zlotys. Its shareholder equity was 763.8 million zlotys, 40 percent more than in 1995.

PBK, one of the nine commercial banks created on the basis of former central bank branches in 1989 as part of the reform of the Polish banking system. It will be the fifth of the group to be privatised.
